[[File:Shadows of the Empire novel cover.jpg|thumb|right|260px|1996 Bantam Spectra hardcover. Art by Drew Struzan.]]

'''Shadows of the Empire''' is a 1996 Lucasfilm multimedia project. The story sits between ''The Empire Strikes Back'' and ''Return of the Jedi''. Lucasfilm released it as a film campaign without producing a film.<ref name="wiki" /><ref name="thrillist" />

== Background ==

In 1994, Bantam editor Lou Aronica proposed a Star Wars crossover to Lucasfilm publishing director Lucy Autrey Wilson. Licensees met at Skywalker Ranch later that year, including author Steve Perry and LucasArts staff.<ref name="wiki" /><ref name="thrillist" /> Lucasfilm producers first wanted a story between ''A New Hope'' and ''The Empire Strikes Back''. ''Dark Forces'' designer Jon Knoles placed it between ''The Empire Strikes Back'' and ''Return of the Jedi'', covering the delivery of Han Solo to Jabba the Hutt.<ref name="thrillist" /><ref name="gameinformer" /> The 1997 Special Editions of the original trilogy followed the campaign.<ref name="wiki" />

Lucasfilm cut a trailer from original-trilogy footage. It played at US comic conventions. Lucasfilm then pulled the trailer so viewers would not expect a theatrical film.<ref name="cavalcade" /> The trailer also aired on QVC.<ref name="thrillist" /> The voiceover said: "After the Empire Strikes Back and before Return of the Jedi, there was a time when heroes and villains alike lived in the Shadows of the Empire."<ref name="irishtimes" />

== Novel ==

Steve Perry wrote the novel for Bantam Spectra. Drew Struzan painted the hardcover. Bantam issued the hardcover in 1996. The novel is the backbone of the project.<ref name="wiki" /><ref name="thrillist" />

Perry's plot follows [[Prince Xizor]], Falleen head of Black Sun, as he tries to kill Luke Skywalker and take Darth Vader's place beside the Emperor. Dash Rendar, a smuggler, stands in for Han Solo while Solo is frozen in carbonite. Leia, Chewbacca, Lando Calrissian, and Luke hunt Boba Fett, fight Tatooine swoop gangs, and raid Xizor's palace on Coruscant.<ref name="wiki" />

== Comic ==

Dark Horse published a six-issue series by John Wagner, with art by Kilian Plunkett. Perry consulted on the story. The comic follows Boba Fett and the other bounty hunters from ''The Empire Strikes Back''. It also follows Jix, a Vader agent inside Jabba's swoop gang. The novel and comic share characters and some scenes. Each tells extra material the other omits.<ref name="wiki" /><ref name="cavalcade" />

== Video game ==

LucasArts developed ''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' for the Nintendo 64. Nintendo published it in North America in December 1996. A Windows port followed in 1997. Mark Haigh-Hutchinson directed. Jon Knoles designed. The player is Dash Rendar.<ref name="gamedev" /><ref name="wiki" />

Levels include the Battle of Hoth, a duel with IG-88, a Mos Eisley swoop chase, the second Death Star plans, and the raid on Xizor's palace. The game sold more than one million copies.<ref name="gamedev" /><ref name="wiki" />

The 1997 Special Edition of ''A New Hope'' includes swoop bikes and Dash Rendar's ship, the [[Outrider]].<ref name="wiki" /><ref name="thrillist" />

== Soundtrack ==

Varèse Sarabande released Joel McNeely's score on 23 April 1996, performed by the Royal Scottish National Orchestra. Drew Struzan painted the album cover. The disc reached stores before the hardcover. The Nintendo 64 and Windows games sample the recording.<ref name="wiki" /><ref name="thrillist" />

== Toys and merchandising ==

Kenner issued action figures and vehicles, including Xizor, Dash Rendar, the ''Outrider'', and a swoop bike. Galoob issued Micro Machines. Topps issued a 100-card set painted by Greg and Tim Hildebrandt. West End Games issued role-playing books.<ref name="wiki" />

== Star Wars CCG ==

Decipher listed a full ''Shadows of the Empire'' expansion in ''[[The Duelist]]'' in 1996. Issue 14 said some planned cards would appear in [[Special Edition]]. Issue 15 reported the expansion canceled. The cancelled expansions keep the title [[Shadows of the Empire]]. [[Special Edition]] printed {{CardLink|Makurth}}, {{CardLink|Flare-S Racing Swoop}}, and {{CardLink|Swoop Mercenary}}.<ref name="duelist13news" /><ref name="duelist14news" /><ref name="duelist15news" />

A later mini-expansion of about 20 cards was advertised for August 2000. The [[Death Star II (expansion)|Death Star II]] starter-deck rulebook named [[Prince Xizor]], [[Dash Rendar]], and their starships. That set never shipped. [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy]] issued those characters as unique premiums, including [[Guri]], [[Outrider]], [[Stinger]], and [[Virago]].<ref name="encyc" />

[[File:Ref2-L-dashrendar.gif|thumb|180px|[[Dash Rendar]], Reflections II.]]

The [[Players Committee]] named its seventh numbered Virtual Set [[Virtual Set 7: Shadows Of The Empire|Shadows Of The Empire]] on 16 July 2004.<ref name="vs7" />
